newsitem.title: UK: BOE's Plenderleith sees stg impact on inflation.
newsitem.headline: BOE's Plenderleith sees stg impact on inflation.

text.p: There will be one-off effects from sterling's appreciation that will affect the recorded inflation rate in the coming months, Bank of England executive director Ian Plenderleith said on Tuesday.
But Plenderleith said it was important "to look further ahead to the medium-term to consider what you think the permanent affects might be on the inflation prospect".
Speaking at a bond conference in London, he added that was why the Bank felt it necessary "to look two years or more ahead in judging what the inflation prospect is".

Plenderleith said one had to take into account the exchange rate rise in sterling and try to assess the reasons underlying the rise -- "which is why we devoted quite a bit of attention to that in our last inflation report".
Governor of the Bank of England Eddie George has called for a rise in official interest rates from the present 6.0 percent, amid fears inflation pressures are building up.

The British government has argued that the strong pound is keeping inflation in check by making imported goods cheaper, and with elections due in May, many economists believe Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke is on course to avoid a rate rise.
Plenderleith cautioned against making snap judgments on monetary policy.
"One has to be careful not to reach a snap judgment that the fact that sterling has risen substitutes for the need for any monetary action in the coming months."
"Plainly the rise in sterling will act as some degree of restraint on the growth of demand and therefore ultimately output in the economy," he said.
"But it comes across from one particular sector and the very difficult judgment one has to make is what will be the effect on that across the economy as a whole in the aggregate level of demand."
"You can't assume that it will produce the degree of restraint that you might judge necessary over that two-year horizon," he said.

Plenderleith said in making any kind of view about the need for interest rate rises, it was important to ask people whether they were confident the inflation target would be achieved, "as that clearly is the objective to which monetary policy is to be directed."
